text: The spec says "ten cfg(test) helpers" and the R-bt-17-MARSHALTESTONLY row lists four marshal helpers, but marshal.rs also has cfg(test)-only skill_defs_from_rows (marshal.rs:497), so eleven dead helpers exist and the DECISIONS amendment should not repeat "ten".

label: a1
text: heal_party consumes its cost item with no trade-lock check, so it spends units that a confirmed session side or a live offer has locked.

label: a1
text: apply_quest_trigger deletes the quest row and then credits the reward through saturating grant_item/grant_currency, so a reward over the cap is clamped away and the quest is marked done.

label: a1
text: ts-6b-3.1 says the write count is not observable from a test, but the native host's Fixture::writes_to observes it, and the tester brief requires asserting it.

label: a2
text: heal_party consumes its cost item one unit at a time with no trade-lock check, so it spends units held by a confirmed session side or a legacy offer.

label: a2
text: apply_quest_trigger deletes the quest row and then credits a reward that grant_item / grant_currency clamp at the cap, so a full stack or wallet silently loses the reward and the quest is marked done.

label: a2
text: ts-6b-3.1 claims the write count is not observable from a test, but native_host_tests::Fixture::writes_to counts every insert/update/delete syscall per table, so the one-write property can be and is gated.

label: a3
text: the ts-6b-3.1 note says the write count is not observable from a test, but the native host counts write syscalls per table and the tests assert exactly one inventory write per debited stack.

label: a5
text: the consume_n contract gives "qty == 0 is Ok" and "no stack is Err" without saying which wins for qty 0 on a missing stack; the test pins Ok.

label: a5
text: heal_party spends the currency cost (first write) before any item check, and the "decide currency first, refuse the item before any write" ordering is unobservable because no shipped heal location charges currency and the cache is not injectable.

label: a5
text: talk upserts player_conversation before apply_quest_trigger runs and advance_dialogue writes player_dialogue_state (npc.rs:443) before apply_effects_to_db, so a refusal after those writes leaves them in the host.

label: a1
text: reachability.test.ts (typed `deps: PointerDeps` at 2517, plus literals at 2652, 2807 and 3070) and menuView.test.ts:334 still pass `choice`/`shop` to PointerSource, but the slice's touches: omits both files, so dropping those deps fails client typecheck (excess properties).

label: a1
text: The spec says to switch the refused-at-battle click to "another refused command the file already uses", but the file's only dispatch-refused vehicle that shows the toast was the deleted dialogue click (menu rows refuse on the menu feedback line, not the toast); the replacement is a click on the hidden Name submit.

label: a1
text: Routing the Shop click through dialogueScreen stamps sentAt even when dispatch sends nothing (no live handle), so the click the test describes as "leaves the button alive" stays dead for DIALOGUE_RESEND_MS; the spec does not say whether that is intended.

label: a2
test: CTL3-6-BOOT-SHOP-NOT-SENT: a Shop click with no live handle sends nothing and leaves the button alive
text: A pick that was never sent (no live handle) still stamps `sentAt`, so the resend guard swallows the next pick for 1 s and the button the spec calls "alive" is dead for that second.

label: a2
text: Once the direct click path is gone, no real control at a battle base dispatches a non-battle-safe command, so the dispatch-wide refusal is reachable end to end only through a stand-in adapter.

label: a2
text: The spec does not say what the router does with the dialogue's 'unhandled' A under a battle; if it falls through to the Deploying base, a dialogue click deploys, and the click half (H.calls must be []) would catch that.

label: a3
text: the 1 s resend guard arms on every A that issues a command, delivered or not (dialogueDismiss SHOP-NOT-SENT needed its retry moved 1 s later), a consequence the ts-6b-5 text does not mention.

label: a3
text: the shipped trees have only idx-0 choices, so the idx-2 argument-shaping check of CTL6B-1-MAIN-DISPATCH cannot be kept through a real click.

label: a4
text: The brief says to switch to "another refused command the file already uses", but main.controls.test.ts has no command reachable at a battle base that reaches dispatch; I used a stand-in dialogue screen returning `care`.

label: a4
text: The "non-numeric data-shop-id sends nothing" arm pins a guard that is deleted with the Shop dep and has no counterpart; I removed the arm and no criterion covers it.

label: a5
text: a Shop A that dispatch did not send (no live handle) still stamps sentAt, so the retry click inside DIALOGUE_RESEND_MS is swallowed; the test now waits 1.1 s, the spec does not say the guard may outlive an unsent command.

label: a5
text: at a battle base a dialogue click now reaches nothing, so the toast refusal of a dialogue click is no longer user-reachable; the refusal coverage rides a stand-in adapter instead.

label: a2
test: A, B and Start pressed while the results wait on the playback each skip it and are consumed, and an A inside the grace of the results show does not continue them
text: outcomeShownAtMs is set at the first syncStack after the frame owner changes, so "the A-grace starts only when the results panel shows" does not say which sync starts it.

label: a4
text: On a battle's first show the shell's own-turn line is queued by tick() via announceNow and then, in the same frame, the overlay-open transition is announced through the trailing-edge LiveRegion (ui/liveRegion.ts:90-95), so the coalescing window keeps only the transition and the turn line the contract says MUST be spoken on that show never reaches #a11y-live.

label: a4
test: a Finished batch waits for the shell playback to drain before the results panel takes the frame
text: The results path sets tacticsShown = null and shows the panel in the Finished batch itself, so the batch's new KO / BattleEnd events never play or speak on the shell, and any line resolved after that falls back to `#<unitId>` names.

label: a5
text: The shell's queued speech goes out through announceNow at tacticsBattle.tick(), BEFORE the same frame's transition edges (l.5349) and countdownSaid (l.5357). The live region keeps only the last write in its 500 ms window, so the KO/finish line spoken on the frame right after a Finished batch (the outcome frame's edge), or a first-sighting own turn with a countdown, is overwritten and never heard, which falls short of ts-6b-7.1's "announce it once".

label: a5
